recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. No core spec edit is needed unless the Security WG later decides to standardize a canonical identifier system or code for specific propagation headers such as b3 or X-Request-Id.
issue_request: FHIR-26923 was a Published Security WG change request with a Persuasive with Modification resolution to add an AuditEvent example showing how internal trace IDs such as Jaeger/b3 propagation identifiers can be recorded using an additional entity and an example.com identifier system.
initial_application: No Jira-tagged commit was found. Git history shows aa9defa3c8 added the AuditEvent examples-list entry for RESTful create with TraceID on 2021-04-07, and dd7da5fcf7 added source/auditevent/audit-event-example-create-traceID.xml the same day.
additional_context: AuditEvent is an active resource in source/fhir.ini, and the examples list references AuditEvent/example-rest-create-traceID. Later AuditEvent model changes, including FHIR-44746, updated field names while preserving the trace-ID entity. The linked Zulip discussion supports representing trace IDs as AuditEvent.entity.what.identifier with object-role Job Stream, and later points users to the current build example. Confluence searches found agenda/minutes references but no contrary final decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because no current source correction is needed. The existing example has a second entity with Identifier.type text TraceID, system http://example.com/server, value 6b507ee2d716780372c255df69ece653, and object-role code 21 Job Stream.

related_jiras.note: Later AuditEvent alignment commit 983d54c76d changed AuditEvent field names in the TraceID example while preserving the trace entity semantics.
